findings.desc: CHK-004 userSees promises: "reviewer_batch and escalation guidance print launch lines like \"lattice host_run --host codex --storyId B-xxxx --agentType reviewer --reviewRunId ... --lane ...\" instead of raw codex exec commands, and docs/host-run-usage.md exists." The doc file (docs/host-run-usage.md) was delivered accurately, but the reviewer_batch guidance was NOT changed at all (git diff main -- packages/main/src/handlers/reviewer-batch.ts is empty) and still only ever emits the in-process Agent(...) subagent launch form (verified live via `lattice reviewer_batch` in this session, e.g. `Agent({ subagent_type: "lattice-review-docs", prompt: "Review story B-70e9 (touchpoints .md)" })`), never `lattice host_run`. review-escalation.ts DID change, but only to add CHK-003 usage-ledger recording (recordHostReadinessProbeUsage) -- it contains no printed guidance-string changes either. The plan.md CHK-004 premise (line 71/79: rewrite raw codex exec / claude --print / agy --print operator-facing instruction strings in these two files) was already false pre-story: `git show main -- reviewer-batch.ts / review-escalation.ts` shows neither file ever printed a raw host-CLI instruction string to rewrite (reviewer_batch only ever used Agent(...); review-escalation.ts had none). CHK-004 evidence notes even acknowledge this ("OQ-2: no raw-launch instruction strings existed to rewrite"), but the checklist userSees text was never corrected to match, so it stands as a literal unfulfilled user-facing promise.
findings.dismissReason: The userSees sentence encodes a premise that was already false before this story: git show main -- packages/main/src/handlers/reviewer-batch.ts / review-escalation.ts contains no raw codex exec / claude --print / agy --print instruction string to rewrite (reviewer_batch has only ever emitted in-session Agent(...) subagent launches, which are deliberately out of scope per CHK-004 verificationIntent edge case). Scope OQ-2 was resolved in writing at PLAN with behavior-based acceptance: the delivered guidance surface is docs/host-run-usage.md (host_run launch lines with binding args for reviewer/quorum host runs) plus the grep-verified absence of raw-launch instruction strings in handlers. userSees text is frozen from DEV by design, so correcting the wording retroactively is not possible without reopening PLAN; the FINDING is accepted as a wording mismatch, not a functional gap. TEST-phase delivery check will verify the doc-based guidance instead.

findings.desc: All 42 must-priority verificationEvidence rows across CHK-001..CHK-007 are currently STALE per lattice validate / evidence_plan (verificationCoverage covered=0/42, missingRequired=42), so the DONE gate would see ZERO valid coverage right now despite the underlying tests genuinely passing. Root cause: evidence was recorded at DEV commit b8d52bbdb (materialHash=9a34267cfc.../storyFilesHash=9df50ebfa3...), then main was merged into story/B-70e9 at 7031fa81c (bringing in an unrelated story B-b264 DONE + a version bump touching package.json/packages/main/package.json), which shifted both materialHash (now 1f57a4081...) and storyFilesHash (now 31513ec6c...) even though none of B-70e9's own story files changed content. Independently confirmed: npm --prefix packages/main run test:host-run-usage (25/25 pass) and test:usage-sweep (11/11 pass) both pass cleanly against current HEAD 867de85e6, and evidence_plan classifies all 42 as refresh-only (hash drift, not rerun_required/hard_stale/missing) -- so this is a re-stamp issue, not a real coverage gap. Needs verification_evidence_refresh_stale / evidence_refresh --apply (or fresh verification_evidence_add) before TEST/DONE so the gate sees the coverage that genuinely exists.
findings.resolvedReason: Ran lattice verification_evidence_refresh_stale for B-70e9 after the deliberate main merge (B-b264 landed on main mid-story; only unrelated version-bump files shifted the whole-tree materialHash/storyFilesHash). evidence_plan now reports missing=0 rerun=0 refresh-only=0 fresh=42. The underlying smokes were independently re-run by the test-coverage reviewer at the post-merge tree (test:host-run-usage 25/25, test:usage-sweep 11/11), so the re-stamp binds passing evidence to the current hashes rather than papering over a real gap.

findings.desc: [codex host-B, cross_host_review B-70e9-xhr-r1] Concurrency cap is check-then-acquire and can be bypassed by concurrent starts: the cap decision scans live slots BEFORE this process creates its own uniquely-named slot file (host-run.ts ~line 570 scan, ~line 605 unconditional acquire of <pid>-<monotonic>.json). Two or more host_run processes starting simultaneously can all observe live < cap, all acquire distinct slots, and all spawn - the documented fail-closed concurrency cap is not enforced under the exact concurrent workload it exists to control. The smoke atomic-race check only exercised wx collision on the SAME filename, which never happens with unique names. Fix direction (codex): fixed numbered slot files slot-0..slot-(cap-1) with exclusive create so only cap contenders can succeed; stale reclaim per slot by pid/mtime.
findings.resolvedReason: Commit 8a8cd2407: replaced check-then-acquire with atomic fixed-numbered slot admission (slot-0..slot-(cap-1), exclusive wx create IS the admission decision; stale reclaim re-probes immediately before unlink and treats lost EEXIST races as moves to the next index, never guaranteed admission). Smoke replaced the fake same-filename race with real contention checks that provably fail against the old primitive: cap=1 second admission without release must return null (old unique-name acquire always succeeded), plus a stale-reclaim race with exactly-one-winner assertion. host-run-usage smoke 27/27; full usage-ledger group green.

findings.desc: [codex host-B, cross_host_review B-70e9-xhr-r1] Blocked codex/agy host runs are recorded as Anthropic usage rows: host_run calls the budget and concurrency block recorders for all three hosts, but those paths use finalContext(), which hard-codes provider.name=anthropic (dispatch-usage.ts ~line 776). A codex or agy hard-budget/concurrency refusal writes its blocked ledger row under the wrong provider, breaking the provider-bound attribution this story claims and corrupting usage diagnostics. Stage A implementer had flagged this as deviation 3 (kept byte-compatible with buildBlockedBudgetRecord); codex confirms it is a real defect. Fix direction: thread the actual host provider into the blocked-record path (provider-parametric contexts for openai/anthropic/antigravity) and add smoke assertions that codex and agy refusals persist provider.name as openai and antigravity respectively.
findings.resolvedReason: Commit 8a8cd2407: buildBlockedBudgetRecord gained a trailing providerName param (default anthropic keeps every legacy caller byte-identical); recordBudgetBlock/recordConcurrencyBlock accept optional provider {name,model}; host_run threads codex->openai / claude->anthropic / agy->antigravity into BOTH blocked paths. Smoke asserts codex budget-block rows carry provider.name=openai, agy concurrency-block rows carry antigravity, and claude blocked rows keep the legacy anthropic shape field-by-field. Would fail against old code which hard-coded anthropic at the builder.

findings.desc: [codex host-B, cross_host_review B-70e9-xhr-r2c] Story-bound host_run ignores configured storyDir: resolvePhase hard-codes .lattice/story/actives (host-run.ts ~line 177) before honoring even an explicit --phase. Projects configuring storyDir in lattice.config.json use the store/config for story metadata everywhere else in the CLI; in such projects every story-bound host_run is refused as unknown story and no host launches. Fix direction: resolve the story via the handler ctx.store (or loadConfig storyDir) and only fail unknown-story against the configured path; when --phase is supplied do not require the index read at all.
findings.resolvedReason: Commit 4f5e980f1: removed the hard-coded .lattice/story/actives read from core; phase resolution goes through an injected HostRunStoryResolver built from ctx.store.readStory in the handler (honors configured storyDir); explicit --phase never consults the store (resolver call count 0 asserted); unknown story via configured store still refuses pre-spawn when no phase is given. New smokes prove the exact old failure modes.

findings.desc: [codex host-B, cross_host_review B-70e9-xhr-r2c] host_run buffers instead of streaming host stdout: the default runner uses spawnSync with piped stdio, withholding all host output until exit, despite the documented contract (docs/host-run-usage.md + CHK-001 DoneWhen: host stdout passes through live, line-streamed, memory-bounded). Long reviewer/quorum runs lose progress observability (the exact B-d8ef complaint) and outputs beyond the 64MiB maxBuffer fail/truncate rather than stream. Fix direction: production runner switches to async spawn, chunks pass through to the caller as they arrive (text mode; json mode routes passthrough to stderr or suppresses it, documented), retaining only bounded data for usage parsing; injected runner seam stays for tests.
findings.resolvedReason: Commit 4f5e980f1: default runner switched to async child_process.spawn with live chunk passthrough (text mode stdout->stdout, json mode->stderr keeping stdout clean), UsageLineScanner retains only the last usage-bearing line capped at 1MiB with honest retentionTruncated -> unavailable on parse miss, no 64MiB maxBuffer, exactly-once delivery (no double print), SIGKILL/timeout semantics preserved. Streaming smoke asserts first line reaches the sink >=80ms before exit; smoke total now 33.

findings.desc: concept-cleanup: F-006 spawnSync-to-async-spawn replacement left a stale forward-looking doc comment: packages/main/src/handlers/host-run.ts:61 CreateHostRunHandlersOptions.runner JSDoc still says 'production uses the piped spawnSync default', but production now uses the async child_process.spawn streaming defaultHostRunRunner (core/host-run.ts). This is not a historical/comparative reference (unlike the two correct comments at core/host-run.ts:715 and tasks/host-run-usage-smoke.ts:566 which explicitly say 'previous'/'old spawnSync') — it is stated as current fact and will mislead future readers of this file changed in this very commit.
